title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on the Implementation of the Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards to Which China Has Acceded

articles.content_en:
Article 4 1. A party applying for recognition and enforcement for the purpose of obtaining the recognition and enforcement referred to in the preceding Article shall, at the time of application, produce:
(a) The original award or a certified copy thereof;
(b) The original agreement referred to in Article 2 or a certified copy thereof.
2. If the said award or agreement is not made in the official language of the country where the award is relied upon, the party applying for recognition and enforcement of the award shall produce a translation of these documents into such language. The translation shall be certified by an official or sworn translator or by a diplomatic or consular agent.

Article 169 The time limit for applying for enforcement shall be one year if both or one of the parties is an individual, and six months if both parties are enterprises, institutions, government organs or organizations.

Article 204 The People's Court of the People's Republic of China shall, pursuant to the international treaties concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China or in accordance with the principle of reciprocity, examine the legally effective judgments and awards entrusted by a foreign court for enforcement. If it considers that such judgments or awards do not violate the basic principles of the laws of the People's Republic of China or the national or social interests of the People's Republic of China, it shall render a ruling to recognize their validity and enforce them in accordance with the procedures provided by this Law. Otherwise, it shall return such judgments or awards to the foreign court.
Annex 3:
States acceding to the Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards:
Denmark (1,2), France (1,2), Greece (1,2), Holy See (1,2), United States of America (1,2), Austria (1), Belgium (1), Federal Republic of Germany (1), Ireland (1), Japan (1), Luxembourg (1), Netherlands (1), Switzerland (1), United Kingdom (1), Norway (1), Australia, Finland, New Zealand (1), San Marino, Spain, Italy, Canada, Sweden, German Democratic Republic (1,2), Hungary (1,2), Poland (1,2), Romania (1,2), Yugoslavia (1,2,3), Bulgaria (1), Czechoslovakia (1), Soviet Union (1), Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic (1), Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic (1), Botswana (1,2), Central African Republic (1,2), China (1,2), Cuba (1,2), Cyprus (1,2), Ecuador (1,2), India (1,2), Indonesia (1,2), Madagascar (1,2), Nigeria (1,2), Philippines (1,2), Trinidad and Tobago (1,2), Tunisia (1,2), Guatemala (1,2), South Korea (1,2), Monaco (1,2), Kuwait (1), Morocco (1), Tanzania (1), Benin, Chile, Colombia, Democratic Kampuchea, Egypt, Ghana, Israel, Jordan, Mexico, Niger, South Africa, Sri Lanka, Syria, Thailand, Uruguay, Djibouti, Haiti, Panama, Malaysia, Singapore.
Notes: 1. That State declares that it will apply the Convention only to arbitral awards made in the territory of another Contracting State, i.e., reciprocity reservation.
2. That State declares that it will apply the Convention only to differences arising out of legal relationships, whether contractual or not, which are considered commercial under its national law, i.e., commercial reservation.
3. That State declares that it will only recognize and enforce arbitral awards made in foreign States after its accession to the Convention.
